newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican fishermen threaten ports blockade.
newsitem.headline: Corsican fishermen threaten ports blockade.

text.p: Corsican fishermen threatened on Sunday to blockade the French Mediterranean island's ports unless they are included in plans to turn the island into a tax haven.
Fishermen unions demanded a halving of payroll taxes and cuts in fuel prices.
"Fishermen are aware...of the economic effects of a blockade but they are determined. It's a matter of survival," said union spokesman Gerard Romiti.

The French National Assembly is to debate on Thursday government plans to exempt most companies in Corsica from corporate taxes and local business tax up to fixed ceilings. Businesses would also receive a partial refund of social security contributions in return for training young people.
The government hopes the plan will boost the local economy, create jobs and appease social discontent that provides a breeding ground for separatists.
The fishermen's threat came on the heels of a 12-day blockade of French roads by truckers who lifted roadblocks last Friday after agreements to meet most of their demands.
